question.html:
Question 13
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[30−72]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j} of R2 under the action of T?

a
[30] and [−72]
b
[3−7] and [02]
c
[−72] and [30]
d
[32] and [0−7]
e
[02] and [3−7]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} are the first and second columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[10]=[3−7]T(j)=T[01]=[02]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} by computing the matrix products T⋅i and T⋅j:

T(i)=T⋅i=[30−72][10]=[3−7]T(j)=T⋅j=[30−72][01]=[02]
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation

observed_steps.name: Question 14
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation
observed_steps.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 14
question.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j\}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 14
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[241−5]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j} of R2 under the action of T?

a
[4−5] and [21]
b
[12] and [−54]
c
[24] and [1−5]
d
[21] and [4−5]
e
[1−5] and [24]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} are the first and second columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[10]=[21]T(j)=T[01]=[4−5]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} by computing the matrix products T⋅i and T⋅j:

T(i)=T⋅i=[241−5][10]=[21]T(j)=T⋅j=[241−5][01]=[4−5]
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation

observed_steps.name: Question 15
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation
observed_steps.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 15
question.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j\}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 1
question.problem: Given that $\{i,j,k\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨6,2,0⟩,$ $⟨-3,5,6⟩,$ and $⟨-1,2,7⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 0 & 6 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

question.html:
Question 1
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨6,2,0⟩, ⟨−3,5,6⟩, and ⟨−1,2,7⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[−127−356620]
b
[620−356−127]
c
[0676−3−1252]
d
[0672526−3−1]
e
[6−3−1252067]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R3 can be represented as a 3×3 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i,j, and k under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is T=[6−3−1252067].
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis

last_observation.name: Question 1
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis
last_observation.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 0 & 6 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

question.name: Question 1
question.problem: Given that $\{i,j,k\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨6,2,0⟩,$ $⟨-3,5,6⟩,$ and $⟨-1,2,7⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 0 & 6 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

question.html:
Question 1
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨6,2,0⟩, ⟨−3,5,6⟩, and ⟨−1,2,7⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[−127−356620]
b
[620−356−127]
c
[0676−3−1252]
d
[0672526−3−1]
e
[6−3−1252067]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R3 can be represented as a 3×3 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i,j, and k under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is T=[6−3−1252067].
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis

solution.reasoning: The standard matrix has columns T(i), T(j), and T(k), respectively, so its rows are (6,-3,-1), (2,5,2), and (0,6,7). This is option e. The captured example supports this method, but no Math Academy answer or grade is captured for the current question.

feedback.name: Question 1
feedback.problem: Given that $\{i,j,k\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨6,2,0⟩,$ $⟨-3,5,6⟩,$ and $⟨-1,2,7⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 0 & 6 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

feedback.html:
Question 1
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨6,2,0⟩, ⟨−3,5,6⟩, and ⟨−1,2,7⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[−127−356620]
b
[620−356−127]
c
[0676−3−1252]
d
[0672526−3−1]
e
[6−3−1252067]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R3 can be represented as a 3×3 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i,j, and k under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is T=[6−3−1252067].
feedback.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis

question.name: Question 2
question.problem: Given that $\{i,j\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$ and that the images of $i$ and $j$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨-1,2⟩$ and $⟨3,-8⟩$, respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

question.html:
Question 2
?

Given that {i,j} is the standard basis of R2 and that the images of i and j under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨−1,2⟩ and ⟨3,−8⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[3−1−82]
b
[3−12−8]
c
[−132−8]
d
[−123−8]
e
[−823−1]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is
T=[−132−8].

question.html:
Question 2
?

Given that {i,j} is the standard basis of R2 and that the images of i and j under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨−1,2⟩ and ⟨3,−8⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[3−1−82]
b
[3−12−8]
c
[−132−8]
d
[−123−8]
e
[−823−1]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is
T=[−132−8].
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis

solution.reasoning: The standard matrix has T(i)=(-1,2) as its first column and T(j)=(3,-8) as its second column, giving option c. The example supports this rule, but no answer key or grade is captured for the current question.

feedback.name: Question 2
feedback.problem: Given that $\{i,j\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$ and that the images of $i$ and $j$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨-1,2⟩$ and $⟨3,-8⟩$, respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

feedback.html:
Question 2
?

Given that {i,j} is the standard basis of R2 and that the images of i and j under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨−1,2⟩ and ⟨3,−8⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[3−1−82]
b
[3−12−8]
c
[−132−8]
d
[−123−8]
e
[−823−1]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is
T=[−132−8].
feedback.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis

question.name: Question 3
question.problem: Given that $\{i,j,k\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨1,-1,3⟩,$ $⟨-4,3,5⟩,$ and $⟨0,-3,1⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -3 \\ 3 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

question.html:
Question 3
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨1,−1,3⟩, ⟨−4,3,5⟩, and ⟨0,−3,1⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[−13−33511−40]
b
[1−40351−13−3]
c
[1−40−13−3351]
d
[−4350−311−13]
e
[1−13−4350−31]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R3 can be represented as a 3×3 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i,j, and k under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is T=[1−40−13−3351].
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis

last_observation.name: Question 3
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis
last_observation.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -3 \\ 3 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

question.name: Question 3
question.problem: Given that $\{i,j,k\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨1,-1,3⟩,$ $⟨-4,3,5⟩,$ and $⟨0,-3,1⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -3 \\ 3 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

question.html:
Question 3
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨1,−1,3⟩, ⟨−4,3,5⟩, and ⟨0,−3,1⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[−13−33511−40]
b
[1−40351−13−3]
c
[1−40−13−3351]
d
[−4350−311−13]
e
[1−13−4350−31]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R3 can be represented as a 3×3 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i,j, and k under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is T=[1−40−13−3351].
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis

solution.reasoning: The standard matrix has columns T(i)=(1,-1,3), T(j)=(-4,3,5), and T(k)=(0,-3,1), giving option c. The captured example supports this method, but no Math Academy answer key or grade is supplied for the current question.

feedback.name: Question 3
feedback.problem: Given that $\{i,j,k\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨1,-1,3⟩,$ $⟨-4,3,5⟩,$ and $⟨0,-3,1⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -3 \\ 3 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

feedback.html:
Question 3
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨1,−1,3⟩, ⟨−4,3,5⟩, and ⟨0,−3,1⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[−13−33511−40]
b
[1−40351−13−3]
c
[1−40−13−3351]
d
[−4350−311−13]
e
[1−13−4350−31]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R3 can be represented as a 3×3 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i,j, and k under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is T=[1−40−13−3351].
feedback.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis

question.name: Question 4
question.problem: Given that $\{i,j\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$ and that the images of $i$ and $j$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨-4,3⟩$ and $⟨5,0⟩$, respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for this linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

question.html:
Question 4
?

Given that {i,j} is the standard basis of R2 and that the images of i and j under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨−4,3⟩ and ⟨5,0⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
 [−4353]
b
 [53−40]
c
 [3−405]
d
 [−4350]
e
 [−4530]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for this linear transformation is T=[−4530].

question.html:
Question 4
?

Given that {i,j} is the standard basis of R2 and that the images of i and j under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨−4,3⟩ and ⟨5,0⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
 [−4353]
b
 [53−40]
c
 [3−405]
d
 [−4350]
e
 [−4530]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for this linear transformation is T=[−4530].
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis

solution.reasoning: The standard matrix places T(i)=(-4,3) in the first column and T(j)=(5,0) in the second column, giving option e. The example supports this method, but no Math Academy answer key or grade is captured for the current question.

feedback.name: Question 4
feedback.problem: Given that $\{i,j\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$ and that the images of $i$ and $j$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨-4,3⟩$ and $⟨5,0⟩$, respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for this linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Given that {i,j} is the standard basis of R2 and that the images of i and j under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨−4,3⟩ and ⟨5,0⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
 [−4353]
b
 [53−40]
c
 [3−405]
d
 [−4350]
e
 [−4530]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for this linear transformation is T=[−4530].

question.name: Question 5
question.problem: Given that $\{i,j,k\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨1,-4,-1⟩,$ $⟨-3,-2,5⟩,$ and $⟨1,0,0⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 \\ -4 & -2 & 0 \\ -1 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

question.html:
Question 5
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨1,−4,−1⟩, ⟨−3,−2,5⟩, and ⟨1,0,0⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[1−310−4−250−1]
b
[1−31−4−20−150]
c
[−4−201−31−150]
d
[1−4−1−3−25100]
e
[1−4−1100−3−25]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R3 can be represented as a 3×3 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i,j, and k under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is T=[1−31−4−20−150].

last_observation.name: Question 5
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis
last_observation.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 \\ -4 & -2 & 0 \\ -1 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

question.name: Question 5
question.problem: Given that $\{i,j,k\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨1,-4,-1⟩,$ $⟨-3,-2,5⟩,$ and $⟨1,0,0⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 \\ -4 & -2 & 0 \\ -1 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

question.html:
Question 5
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨1,−4,−1⟩, ⟨−3,−2,5⟩, and ⟨1,0,0⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[1−310−4−250−1]
b
[1−31−4−20−150]
c
[−4−201−31−150]
d
[1−4−1−3−25100]
e
[1−4−1100−3−25]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R3 can be represented as a 3×3 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i,j, and k under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is T=[1−31−4−20−150].
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis

solution.reasoning: The standard matrix has columns T(i)=(1,-4,-1), T(j)=(-3,-2,5), and T(k)=(1,0,0), giving option b. The example supports this method, but no Math Academy answer key or grade is captured for the current question.

feedback.name: Question 5
feedback.problem: Given that $\{i,j,k\}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨1,-4,-1⟩,$ $⟨-3,-2,5⟩,$ and $⟨1,0,0⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 \\ -4 & -2 & 0 \\ -1 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

feedback.html:
Question 5
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨1,−4,−1⟩, ⟨−3,−2,5⟩, and ⟨1,0,0⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[1−310−4−250−1]
b
[1−31−4−20−150]
c
[−4−201−31−150]
d
[1−4−1−3−25100]
e
[1−4−1100−3−25]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R3 can be represented as a 3×3 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i,j, and k under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is T=[1−31−4−20−150].
feedback.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis

question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156544/assets/2f0c94bc3100b4fd9754ee822f55e2edbae8475bece3b18ac34f63e6c92267a2.png)

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

last_observation.name: Question 6
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given a Diagram
last_observation.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156544/assets/2f0c94bc3100b4fd9754ee822f55e2edbae8475bece3b18ac34f63e6c92267a2.png)

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:

${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

question.html:
Question 6
?

In the diagram above, i and j are the vectors of the standard basis of R2, while i′ and j′ are their images under the linear transformation T. What is the standard matrix of T?

a
[123−3]
b
[312−3]
c
[31−32]
d
[3−312]
e
[132−3]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that i′=[3−3] and j′=[12].

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

T=[31−32].
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given a Diagram

solution.reasoning: The current diagram shows T(i)=(3,-3) and T(j)=(1,2). Placing these images in the first and second columns gives option c. No Math Academy answer key or grade is captured for this question.

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156544/assets/2f0c94bc3100b4fd9754ee822f55e2edbae8475bece3b18ac34f63e6c92267a2.png)

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

question.html:
Question 7
?

In the diagram above, i and j are the vectors of the standard basis of R2, while i′ and j′ are their images under the linear transformation T. What is the standard matrix of T?

a
[23−11]
b
[312−1]
c
[2−131]
d
[2−113]
e
[−1123]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that i′=[23] and j′=[−11].

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

T=[2−131].

last_observation.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

In the diagram above,  $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and  ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

question.html:
Question 7
?

In the diagram above, i and j are the vectors of the standard basis of R2, while i′ and j′ are their images under the linear transformation T. What is the standard matrix of T?

a
[23−11]
b
[312−1]
c
[2−131]
d
[2−113]
e
[−1123]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that i′=[23] and j′=[−11].

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

T=[2−131].
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given a Diagram

solution.reasoning: The current diagram shows T(i)=(2,3) and T(j)=(-1,1). These form the first and second columns of the standard matrix, giving option c. No Math Academy answer key or grade is captured for this question.

[−1123]

question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156544/assets/20aff9b0dd1ea6aaab8cfa932317e83015956ac355349d5ae3d744de289bdae5.png)

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

last_observation.name: Question 8
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given a Diagram
last_observation.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156544/assets/20aff9b0dd1ea6aaab8cfa932317e83015956ac355349d5ae3d744de289bdae5.png)

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$

question.html:
Question 8
?

In the diagram above, i and j are the vectors of the standard basis of R2, while i′ and j′ are their images under the linear transformation T. What is the standard matrix of T?

a
[31−12]
b
[−1231]
c
[−1321]
d
[3−121]
e
[3−112]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that i′=[31] and j′=[−12].

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

T=[3−112].
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given a Diagram

solution.reasoning: The current diagram shows T(i)=(3,1) and T(j)=(-1,2). Placing these vectors as the first and second columns gives option e. No Math Academy answer key or grade is captured for this question.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156544/assets/20aff9b0dd1ea6aaab8cfa932317e83015956ac355349d5ae3d744de289bdae5.png)

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

question.html:
Question 9
?

In the diagram above, i and j are the vectors of the standard basis of R2, while i′ and j′ are their images under the linear transformation T. What is the standard matrix of T?

a
 [21−23]
b
 [−2321]
c
 [−2123]
d
[−2231]
e
 [2−213]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that i′=[−23] and j′=[21].

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

T=[−2231].

last_observation.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

In the diagram above,  $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and  ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

question.html:
Question 9
?

In the diagram above, i and j are the vectors of the standard basis of R2, while i′ and j′ are their images under the linear transformation T. What is the standard matrix of T?

a
 [21−23]
b
 [−2321]
c
 [−2123]
d
[−2231]
e
 [2−213]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that i′=[−23] and j′=[21].

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

T=[−2231].
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given a Diagram

solution.reasoning: The current diagram shows T(i)=(-2,3) and T(j)=(2,1). These images form the first and second columns of the standard matrix, giving option d. No Math Academy answer key or grade is captured for this question.

a
 [21−23]
b
 [−2321]
c
 [−2123]
d
[−2231]
e
 [2−213]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

question.name: Question 10
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156544/assets/ad1f032fd5b99252d348d0cf71308ef1de0f65f06ddd9070b569cff69bc506f9.png)

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

last_observation.name: Question 10
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given a Diagram
last_observation.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156544/assets/ad1f032fd5b99252d348d0cf71308ef1de0f65f06ddd9070b569cff69bc506f9.png)

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$

question.html:
Question 10
?

In the diagram above, i and j are the vectors of the standard basis of R2, while i′ and j′ are their images under the linear transformation T. What is the standard matrix of T?

a
 [112−1]
b
 [12−1−1]
c
 [−1−112]
d
[1−12−1]
e
[−121−1]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that i′=[12] and j′=[−1−1].

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

T=[1−12−1].
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given a Diagram

solution.reasoning: The current diagram shows T(i)=(1,2) and T(j)=(-1,-1). These images form the first and second columns of the standard matrix, giving option d. No Math Academy answer key or grade is captured for this question.

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156544/assets/ad1f032fd5b99252d348d0cf71308ef1de0f65f06ddd9070b569cff69bc506f9.png)

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

question.name: Question 11
question.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j,k\}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i,$ $T\cdot j,$ and $T\cdot k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T\cdot k=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[1−2341−1110]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j,k} of R3 under the action of T?

a
 [1−23], [41−1], and [110]
b
 [141], [−211], and [3−10]
c
 [123], [41−1], and [110]
d
 [141], [2−11], and [310]
e
 [114], [−211], and [30−1]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} are the first, second, and third columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[100]=[141]T(j)=T[010]=[−211]T(k)=T[001]=[3−10]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} by computing the matrix products T⋅i, T⋅j, and T⋅k:

T(i)=T⋅i=[1−2341−1110][100]=[141]T(j)=T⋅j=[1−2341−1110][010]=[−211]T(k)=T⋅k=[1−2341−1110][001]=[3−10]

last_observation.name: Question 11
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation
last_observation.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i,$ $T\cdot j,$ and $T\cdot k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T\cdot k=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 11
question.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j,k\}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$

question.html:
Question 11
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[1−2341−1110]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j,k} of R3 under the action of T?

a
 [1−23], [41−1], and [110]
b
 [141], [−211], and [3−10]
c
 [123], [41−1], and [110]
d
 [141], [2−11], and [310]
e
 [114], [−211], and [30−1]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} are the first, second, and third columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[100]=[141]T(j)=T[010]=[−211]T(k)=T[001]=[3−10]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} by computing the matrix products T⋅i, T⋅j, and T⋅k:

T(i)=T⋅i=[1−2341−1110][100]=[141]T(j)=T⋅j=[1−2341−1110][010]=[−211]T(k)=T⋅k=[1−2341−1110][001]=[3−10]
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation

solution.reasoning: Multiplying by i, j, and k selects the first, second, and third columns of T, respectively. Thus the images are (1,4,1), (-2,1,1), and (3,-1,0), matching option b. No Math Academy answer key or grade is captured for this question.

feedback.name: Question 11
feedback.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j,k\}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i,$ $T\cdot j,$ and $T\cdot k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T\cdot k=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[1−2341−1110]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j,k} of R3 under the action of T?

a
 [1−23], [41−1], and [110]
b
 [141], [−211], and [3−10]
c
 [123], [41−1], and [110]
d
 [141], [2−11], and [310]
e
 [114], [−211], and [30−1]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} are the first, second, and third columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[100]=[141]T(j)=T[010]=[−211]T(k)=T[001]=[3−10]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} by computing the matrix products T⋅i, T⋅j, and T⋅k:

T(i)=T⋅i=[1−2341−1110][100]=[141]T(j)=T⋅j=[1−2341−1110][010]=[−211]T(k)=T⋅k=[1−2341−1110][001]=[3−10]

question.name: Question 12
question.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j,k\}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i,$ $T\cdot j,$ and $T\cdot k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T\cdot k=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 12
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[1−4−1−35−20−10]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j,k} of R3 under the action of T?

a
[−310], [5−4−1], and [−2−10]
b
[1−30], [−45−1], and [−1−20]
c
[−35−2], [1−4−1], and [0−10]
d
[−45−1], [1−30], and [−1−20]
e
[1−4−1], [−35−2], and [0−10]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} are the first, second, and third columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[100]=[1−30]T(j)=T[010]=[−45−1]T(k)=T[001]=[−1−20]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} by computing the matrix products T⋅i, T⋅j, and T⋅k:

T(i)=T⋅i=[1−4−1−35−20−10][100]=[1−30]T(j)=T⋅j=[1−4−1−35−20−10][010]=[−45−1]T(k)=T⋅k=[1−4−1−35−20−10][001]=[−1−20]

last_observation.name: Question 12
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation
last_observation.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

question.name: Question 12
question.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j,k\}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i,$ $T\cdot j,$ and $T\cdot k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T\cdot k=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 12
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[1−4−1−35−20−10]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j,k} of R3 under the action of T?

a
[−310], [5−4−1], and [−2−10]
b
[1−30], [−45−1], and [−1−20]
c
[−35−2], [1−4−1], and [0−10]
d
[−45−1], [1−30], and [−1−20]
e
[1−4−1], [−35−2], and [0−10]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} are the first, second, and third columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[100]=[1−30]T(j)=T[010]=[−45−1]T(k)=T[001]=[−1−20]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} by computing the matrix products T⋅i, T⋅j, and T⋅k:

T(i)=T⋅i=[1−4−1−35−20−10][100]=[1−30]T(j)=T⋅j=[1−4−1−35−20−10][010]=[−45−1]T(k)=T⋅k=[1−4−1−35−20−10][001]=[−1−20]
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation

solution.reasoning: Multiplication by i, j, and k selects the first, second, and third columns of T, respectively. The images are (1,-3,0), (-4,5,-1), and (-1,-2,0), matching option b. No Math Academy answer key or grade is captured for this question.

feedback.name: Question 12
feedback.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j,k\}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i,$ $T\cdot j,$ and $T\cdot k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T\cdot k=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

Question 12
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[1−4−1−35−20−10]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j,k} of R3 under the action of T?

a
[−310], [5−4−1], and [−2−10]
b
[1−30], [−45−1], and [−1−20]
c
[−35−2], [1−4−1], and [0−10]
d
[−45−1], [1−30], and [−1−20]
e
[1−4−1], [−35−2], and [0−10]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} are the first, second, and third columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[100]=[1−30]T(j)=T[010]=[−45−1]T(k)=T[001]=[−1−20]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} by computing the matrix products T⋅i, T⋅j, and T⋅k:

T(i)=T⋅i=[1−4−1−35−20−10][100]=[1−30]T(j)=T⋅j=[1−4−1−35−20−10][010]=[−45−1]T(k)=T⋅k=[1−4−1−35−20−10][001]=[−1−20]

question.name: Question 13
question.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j\}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 13
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[30−72]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j} of R2 under the action of T?

a
[30] and [−72]
b
[3−7] and [02]
c
[−72] and [30]
d
[32] and [0−7]
e
[02] and [3−7]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} are the first and second columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[10]=[3−7]T(j)=T[01]=[02]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} by computing the matrix products T⋅i and T⋅j:

T(i)=T⋅i=[30−72][10]=[3−7]T(j)=T⋅j=[30−72][01]=[02]

last_observation.name: Question 13
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation
last_observation.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 13
question.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j\}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 13
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[30−72]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j} of R2 under the action of T?

a
[30] and [−72]
b
[3−7] and [02]
c
[−72] and [30]
d
[32] and [0−7]
e
[02] and [3−7]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} are the first and second columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[10]=[3−7]T(j)=T[01]=[02]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} by computing the matrix products T⋅i and T⋅j:

T(i)=T⋅i=[30−72][10]=[3−7]T(j)=T⋅j=[30−72][01]=[02]
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation

solution.reasoning: Multiplication by i and j selects the first and second columns of T, respectively. Thus T(i)=(3,-7) and T(j)=(0,2), matching option b. No Math Academy answer key or grade is captured for this question.

feedback.name: Question 13
feedback.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j\}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.html:
Question 13
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[30−72]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j} of R2 under the action of T?

a
[30] and [−72]
b
[3−7] and [02]
c
[−72] and [30]
d
[32] and [0−7]
e
[02] and [3−7]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} are the first and second columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[10]=[3−7]T(j)=T[01]=[02]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} by computing the matrix products T⋅i and T⋅j:

T(i)=T⋅i=[30−72][10]=[3−7]T(j)=T⋅j=[30−72][01]=[02]

question.name: Question 14
question.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j\}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 14
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[241−5]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j} of R2 under the action of T?

a
[4−5] and [21]
b
[12] and [−54]
c
[24] and [1−5]
d
[21] and [4−5]
e
[1−5] and [24]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} are the first and second columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[10]=[21]T(j)=T[01]=[4−5]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} by computing the matrix products T⋅i and T⋅j:

T(i)=T⋅i=[241−5][10]=[21]T(j)=T⋅j=[241−5][01]=[4−5]

last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation
last_observation.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

[24] and [1−5]

[1−5] and [24]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} are the first and second columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[10]=[21]T(j)=T[01]=[4−5]

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} by computing the matrix products T⋅i and T⋅j:

feedback.name: Question 14
feedback.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j\}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 15
question.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j\}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 15
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[4−451]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j} of R2 under the action of T?

a
 [−45] and [41]
b
 [45] and [−41]
c
 [−41] and [45]
d
 [4−4] and [51]
e
 [41] and [−45]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} are the first and second columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[10]=[45]T(j)=T[01]=[−41]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} by computing the matrix products T⋅i and T⋅j:

T(i)=T⋅i=[4−451][10]=[45]T(j)=T⋅j=[4−451][01]=[−41]
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation

last_observation.name: Question 15
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation
last_observation.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 15
question.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j\}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 15
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[4−451]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j} of R2 under the action of T?

a
 [−45] and [41]
b
 [45] and [−41]
c
 [−41] and [45]
d
 [4−4] and [51]
e
 [41] and [−45]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} are the first and second columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[10]=[45]T(j)=T[01]=[−41]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} by computing the matrix products T⋅i and T⋅j:

T(i)=T⋅i=[4−451][10]=[45]T(j)=T⋅j=[4−451][01]=[−41]
question.knowledge_point: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation

solution.reasoning: Multiplication by i and j selects the first and second columns of T, respectively. Thus T(i)=(4,5) and T(j)=(-4,1), matching option b. No Math Academy answer key or grade is captured for this question.

feedback.name: Question 15
feedback.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j\}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
